source.title: Interpreting Deep Visual Representations via Network Dissection
source.authors: Bo-Lei Zhou; David Bau; A. Oliva; A. Torralba

record.tranche_reason: The study measures alignment of individual visual-network units with labeled concepts, not similarity between representations of the same inputs or recurrence of shared features across models. Its seed comparison reports similar interpretability levels, not shared features or subspaces.
record.gate_note: The paper cites convergent learning and reports a related comparison across random initializations. That result concerns levels of unit interpretability, not the convergence versions in the claim. Its rotation, architecture, training-task, and threshold results likewise measure unit-to-concept interpretability rather than model-to-model representational convergence.
record.test_reason: Network Dissection scores how well single units align with labelled concepts within each network. It never compares two models' representations of the same inputs, and never matches specific units or features across models. The seed comparison (Sec. 3.6, Fig. 17) reports only aggregate detector counts. The authors say this matches convergent learning [21], but it does not test whether the same features are learned.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that units are far more interpretable than a random basis, that interpretability is axis-aligned and is destroyed by rotation without loss of accuracy, and that it varies with architecture, supervision, training conditions and width. They also conclude it carries information that classification performance alone does not.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses unit-to-concept segmentation alignment; it does not apply a method for measuring convergence between independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: Unit-interpretability results depend on the concept vocabulary and the activation threshold; varying the threshold changes which concepts are assigned to units.

fits_no_version.finding: AlexNet trained on Places205 from three random initializations reaches similar numbers of unique and total concept detectors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different seeds give similar aggregate unit interpretability. This does not establish that they learn the same features.

fits_no_version.finding: Each of five architectures trained on Places365 has units that act as detectors for the same Broden concepts (e.g., bus, airplane, dog). Detector quality and appearance differ across networks (Fig. 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-unit detectors for the same labelled concepts emerge across CNN architectures. This is evidence of shared concept coverage under a fixed vocabulary, not of matched features.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The seed comparison is qualitative in the text and does not report uncertainty. The measured construct is individual-unit alignment with a labeled vocabulary, not cross-model representational similarity.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows were included because the reported architecture, rotation, training-task, and threshold results measure unit-to-concept interpretability rather than any listed convergence version.

untested.parts: No cross-model similarity measured as a function of scale or capability.
No image-caption alignment between vision and language models. The captioning model in Sec. 3.5 is dissected alone.
Seeds are compared only on aggregate interpretability counts, not on shared units, features or subspaces.
No mapping or stitching between models is tested.
Concept detectors such as bus and airplane appear in each architecture (Fig. 11), but units are never matched across models and recurrence is never quantified.
Threshold and vocabulary dependence apply to the interpretability score, not to a convergence measure.
No measure of the degree of cross-model alignment, and no test of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: I agree with the record's T6/discusses call. Within-model fine-tuning keeps 54.4% (ImageNet to Places) and 52.7% (Places to ImageNet) of conv5 concepts, but that is not a comparison of independently trained models. The rotation result concerns the basis within one model, not across models.

versions.untested_parts: Not tested whether distances between inputs become more similar across independently trained models as size or capability increases.
No vision-language alignment of paired images and captions.
Different initializations are compared only for levels of interpretability, not for shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative representation, or unpaired alignment between models is tested.
The paper compares unit-concept interpretability across networks but does not measure recurrence or overlap of the same features or circuits across models.
The paper varies its unit-interpretability scoring settings, not a measure of convergence between models.
No partial or plateauing cross-model alignment, or causal role of shared data or objectives in such alignment, is tested.

rows.subject: Repeat1, Repeat2, Repeat3 (reported together)
rows.operation_detail: Compared unit interpretability across random initializations of AlexNet trained on Places205.
rows.value: The models converge to similar levels of interpretability on both measures.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative comparison of interpretability levels, not a comparison of learned features or model-to-model distances.
rows.check: The measure is aggregate counts of unique and total detectors across three random initializations. It does not show whether the seeds share features or subspaces, so it cannot bear on V3. The value is qualitative only and has no uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
